title: Count number of subarrays with given xor K
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Count subarrays whose XOR equals K.
intuition: XOR behaves like addition with its own inverse: xor(i..j) = pre[j] ^ pre[i-1]. Setting that equal to K gives pre[i-1] = pre[j] ^ K — the exact same map lookup as the sum version.

approaches.title: Brute: all subarrays
Optimal: prefix XOR counts
approaches.idea: Seed {0: 1}; add freq[pre ^ k] at each step.
approaches.code:
from collections import defaultdict


def count_subarrays_xor_k(a: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    freq = defaultdict(int)
    freq[0] = 1
    pre = 0
    count = 0
    for x in a:
        pre ^= x
        count += freq[pre ^ k]
        freq[pre] += 1
    return count

approaches.whyWorks: pre[j] ^ K = pre[i-1] is an equivalence, because XOR is its own inverse.

commonMistakes: Using pre - k instead of pre ^ k
patternRecognition: Any invertible associative operation supports the prefix + hash-map trick
interviewInsight: Saying "XOR is self-inverse, so the sum template transfers verbatim" is the insight they want.
